abstract: Cell-type-specific gene silencing mediated by H3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me3)-marked chromatin is a conserved strategy for securing cell fate. In Drosophila germ cells, H3K9 methylation plays a crucial role in maintaining female identity by silencing testis-specific transcription of the PHD finger protein 7 (phf7) gene. However, the molecular mechanism underlying installation of this epigenetic mark remains poorly understood. Our prior work established that H3K9me3 installation requires the SETDB1 H3K9 methyltransferase and the DNA-binding protein Identity Crisis (IDC), a member of the ZAD-ZNF protein family. Here, we establish that the multifunctional DNA-binding protein Stonewall (STWL) is also essential for H3K9me3 deposition. Like IDC, STWL binds to chromatin within the first non-coding exon of phf7. To identify additional phf7 regulators, we leveraged mass spectrometry data on STWL- and IDC-associated proteins from ovarian lysates, prioritizing candidates enriched in both datasets. Notably, we observed enrichment of WINDEI (WDE), a required SETDB1 co-factor, suggesting that STWL and IDC may directly recruit SETDB1 to phf7 through their shared interaction with WDE. Another common interactor, the newly identified member of the ZAD-ZNF protein family called PUTZIG (PZG), also localizes to the first non-coding exon, where it promotes H3K9me3 deposition and silencing. Lastly, we show that PZG and IDC binding to the phf7 locus depends on the female sex-determination gene Sex-lethal. Collectively, our findings support a model in which IDC, STWL, and PZG, though individually insufficient, determine lineage choice by collectively producing a stable, locus-specific recruitment platform for H3K9me3 deposition in female but not male germ cells.

summary: In Drosophila female germ cells, IDC, STWL and PZG cooperatively recruit SETDB1 via WDE to deposit H3K9me3 silencing at phf7, controlling female identity.
title: Identity Crisis, Stonewall, and Putzig control the installation of a locus-specific H3K9me3 silencing domain essential for female germ cell identity in Drosophila.
